messages.author: 3908a2da5354fc44
messages.subject: Df for Pooled Estimates
parts:
My question relates to how the df are calculated for the pooled
estimates of density.

I am conducting analyses for 3 species of grassland songbirds. We had 2
observers who surveyed different transects so, of course, we are
interested if there are differences in detection functions between
observers. Consequently, we post-stratified on observer. Also, we
pooled data for a global detection function and compared AIC values for
separate versus global detection functions. From what I can tell this
is ok as long as the same data, cutpoints, etc. are used (in all cases
we used exact distances in our analysis) - when you compare 2 detection
functions to a global detection function you simply sum the 2 AIC values
to compare to the global model.

For one species we found that a single global detection function had a
lesser AIC value than if we estimated a detection function for each
observer. Therefore, we did not post-stratify and the df=376 for the
global density estimate. We had 252 transects and 147 observations
(hazard rate detection function with no adjustments). Where does 376
come from?

If we use a global detection function, post-stratify on observer, and
estimate a global density (mean weighted by line length), I get df=4.
Why not df=1 (no. observers - 1) if I am using an empirical variance?
For these same data I found that if I estimate separate detection
functions and post-stratify the global estimate has df=1.

For the other two species of songbirds each observer had a different
shaped detection function (the exact same function was selected for each
observer, just the parameter estimates differed). The df for these
pooled estimates (empirical variance, estimate is mean of strata
weighted by line length) appears to be df=(no. observers)-1 = 2-1 = 1.
Correct?

Sorry if this question has been addressed previously on the listserve,
but I searched the archives and could not find anything on this topic.

Thanks,

Duane
